page.layout: One printed page of running text, with a narrow margin of notes on the left. No heading. Running head at top centre, page number at top left. Catchword "quod" at lower right.

main_text.p: Apostro-phe ad om- nes omnium gentium Ec-clesias quæ Antichristi- su Roma-num eiura- runt.si vera sunt, id est, omnibus Christianæ nostrę religionis capitibus, Apostolico symbolo, quod est totius divinæ Scripturæ epitome, divinitus dictato, comprehensis penitus consentanea: cur non omnes, quaeso, & singuli, quibus Deus ad agnoscendum magis ac magis Antichristum oculos aperuit, in hanc veritatem consentimus? Sin vero, ista vel penitus vel aliquatenus ab illa veritate discrepant, cur odiis, calumniis, virulentis denique omnibus conuitiis semel conceptas opiniones non sane constanter, sed quoquo modo retinentes, alij alios lacerare tamdiu malumus, quàm nos mutuò per illum placidissimum Christi spiritum, in sacro & legitimo conuentu [illegible, ~8 letters], & sic mutua Christiana ὁμοφρο-σύνῃ communes illos veritatis hostes, vel ad eiusdem veritatis consensionem pertrahere, vel magis ac magis arguere? Et qua de re potius vere Christianos omnes Reges, Principes, Magistratus denique cæteros, & quidé in primis Ecclesiarū Pastores laborare oportuit: Cur non, inquam, illud ipsum ultro inter nos agimus, quod toties à Pontificiis ipsis tato studio impetrare studuimus, nempe ut placidè nobiscum de controversiis religionis, ex puro Dei verbo, in libera & legitima Synodo conferre mallent, quàm innoxios, & ultrò fidei suæ confessionem edere, & tali collationi, cui Deus ipse præsideret sese subiicere paratos, omnis crudelitatis genere persequi? Hoc verò tantum & tam necessarium beneficium quod

page.notes: Line 1 of the main text: the word after "conuentu" is Greek, printed "vu&elev" in the scan, and I cannot read its letters reliably, so it is marked illegible. The first word of the page is a fragment, "fi", taken as "si" (long s). "tato" in "ipsis tato studio" is printed as shown and looks like a misprint for "tanto". The left margin note contains printed line-end hyphens, kept as printed. The "su" in the note after "Antichristi-" is doubtful. The Greek "ὁμοφρο-σύνῃ" is split across the line end at the printed hyphen.
